key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving electronic uniformity, showing that morphology and optoelectronic quality can be decoupled.
engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a route to more durable perovskite photovoltaics without requiring smoother film surfaces.
method: Cap 3D perovskites with Ruddlesden–Popper layers derived from 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium.
Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare pristine and capped films before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films showed enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, with better preservation of optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative device-efficiency or operational-lifetime results, so film-level improvements should not be equated with proven solar-cell durability.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
